newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says Hebron deal face-saving for U.S..
newsitem.headline: Iran says Hebron deal face-saving for U.S..

text.p: A deal on Palestinian self-rule in the West Bank town of Hebron was only a face-saving agreement for U.S. and other mediators, Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said in remarks broadcast on Thursday.

Velayati said in an interview with Cable News Network (CNN) television that Arab states were coming to the same belief as Iran -- that the Middle East peace process ..."is not sufficient and is not enough for making real peace in the Middle East".

"...Now you see the peace process in the Middle East is in a deadlock and after a long period of shuttle diplomacy between several countries, mainly by the special representative of the United States in the Middle East Mr Dennis Ross, all of a sudden I heard that an agreement about the partial withdrawal of the Israeli forces from Hebron has been signed," Velayati said.

"I don't think this is a real peace agreement which could solve the very complicated problems of Palestine. This is only for propaganda or face-saving for those who have been involved in this shuttle diplomacy between different parties," he added.

Asked about Iran's support for Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas waging attacks on Israeli forces from Lebanon at a time when Arab states and Israel were involved in the peace process, Velayati said: "...The Iranian authorities have said repeatedly when we are expressing our views it does not mean that we are going to disturb any peace agreement in any place in the Middle East or other places practically. We only express our views."
Hizbollah leads an Islamic Resistance committed to ousting Israeli troops and their allies from a 15-km (nine miles)-wide south Lebanon occupation zone.

"What happened in the last two years has proved that Iran is right and you can see that there is a disappointment in more or less all Middle East Arab countries -- those who used to be very optimistic about this peace process, the important countries, the major Arab countries in the region now have expressed their pessimism about the peace process," he added.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat bowed to weeks of U.S. pressure and sealed the accord at a late-night summit on Tuesday and agreed on a timeframe for further Israeli pullbacks in the West Bank.

Hebron, a West Bank flashpoint, is home to 400 militant Jewish settlers and 100,000 Arabs. It was due to be given self-rule 10 months ago but violence, security concerns and Israel's change of government in June delayed the pullback.
